A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IBISAgent and contain readable main text and supplementary material, including Appendices A–F. Text, equations, tables, figures, and relocated appendix content can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation comparisons, training and reward ablations, inference timings, VQA results, and qualitative case studies in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports an RL training-reward trajectory in Appendix D.6 and Figure 13.

M1.justification: The iterative reasoning/click/mask procedure, Qwen2.5-VL backbone, segmentation tools, reflective trajectory synthesis, SFT/GRPO training, and reward functions are unchanged. Revisions to dataset descriptions do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: The represented datasets, modalities, segmentation tasks, VQA tasks, and error-handling scenarios remain unchanged. Both appendices already specify eight in-domain test modalities; removing the conflicting nine-modality statement from Section 4.1 does not establish a coverage reduction.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the segmentation, prompted-agent, VQA, tool-replacement, and standalone-tool comparisons (Tables 1, 3, and 8–10). No evaluated baseline is added or removed.

E3.justification: The main text revises the in-domain test count from 3K to 9K and RL pixel-level/total QA counts from 562K/886K to 564K/888K, and removes the claim that RL samples exclude SFT samples. Both appendices already report 9,902 test samples, 564,385 pixel-level RL QAs, and some SFT/RL overlap. These are limited corrections to reported settings; the PDFs do not establish rerunning or repartitioning experiments.

E4.justification: New Appendix D.6 and Figure 13 examine reward evolution during RL training. Existing training-stage, reward-component, and segmentation-tool ablations, along with qualitative robustness and error-correction cases, are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 13 newly reports descriptive reward statistics, including a standard deviation of 0.1222 over the displayed 220-step trajectory. This adds within-trajectory variability reporting, not uncertainty across independent runs. No seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: New Figure 13 reports an IoU-reward trajectory with mean 2.2593, maximum 2.6880 at step 215, and final value 2.5900. Existing benchmark scores, rankings, ablation results, timings, and qualitative examples remain unchanged; no same-setting benchmark performance gain is reported.

T1.justification: The rollout formulation, optimization objective, trajectory-generation equations, and reward definitions in Equations 1–14 are unchanged. Equation relocation introduces no new mathematical reasoning, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction revises the claimed trajectory-dataset scale from 640K to 400K+, consistent with the previously reported 456,795 QA pairs. The central claims about architecture-preserving segmentation, iterative reasoning, two-stage training, and superior performance remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix D.6 newly interprets the reward trajectory as evidence of stable training and progressively improved planning and segmentation. Appendix A.2.2 removes the assertion that main-paper ablations validate the hybrid training-data configuration. Existing limitations concerning 2D operation and interaction efficiency remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Figure 13 newly documents a 220-step RL trace, without stating a change to the existing 12-epoch training budget. Hardware, learning rates, batch sizes, trajectory-generation pseudocode, prompts, and the promise of public dataset/code/model release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including the comparison with segmentation-token methods and single-turn tool-using MLLMs. Changes to bibliography page backlinks reflect relocated content, not added or removed references.

P1.justification: v3 adds the short RL Training Dynamics subsection and makes localized count corrections, a sentence deletion, and cross-reference updates. The overall narrative, section organization, and most wording remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds the reward-curve Figure 13, moves the existing modality-distribution Figure 4 from PDF page 13 to page 12, and adjusts appendix text flow. The existing prompt figure becomes Figure 14 and the dataset-breakdown figure becomes Figure 15; their content is retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves internal consistency by correcting main-text dataset counts and removing the SFT/RL-disjointness statement that contradicted Appendix A. It also removes an unsupported claim of data-mixture ablation support and adds a training diagnostic. These improve reporting and transparency, but the unchanged benchmark evidence and absence of uncertainty across independent runs keep the overall gain limited.
